ops.note: Prose ⟶ lines turn every ؟ (and ،) into ? (and ,), even when the sign itself is the thing being explained. Rule: in a prose ⟶ line, an Arabic punctuation mark that stands alone (between spaces / Latin text, not attached to an Arabic word) is kept as the Arabic sign; a mark attached to an Arabic word stays sentence punctuation and is still mapped. Code: the punct maps in src/lang/ar/tap.ts (lines ~279, ~348, ~391) and src/core/translit.ts PUNCT (line ~72). Examples: (1) grammar [5].explanation 'The Arabic question mark ؟ is a mirrored ?.' must read '... question mark ؟ is a mirrored ?.' (now '... question mark ? is a mirrored ?.'); (2) vocabulary note (audit/vocabulary.txt:17514) 'The Arabic comma ، and question mark ؟ face the other way.' must keep ، and ؟ (now ', ' and '?'); (3) unchanged: هَلْ أَنْتَ مِصْرِيّ؟ still reads 'hal anta miṣrī?'.

ops.note: A bare hamza-seat letter shown on its own (أ, إ, ؤ, ئ with no harakat) must transliterate as 'ʾ', like ء (src/core/translit.ts). Now: أ ؤ ئ give an empty ⟶ and إ gives 'I'. Examples: pronunciation.json [13] (hamza page) letters[1] أ → 'ʾ' (now empty), letters[2] إ → 'ʾ' (now 'I'), letters[4] ئ → 'ʾ' (now empty); letters[0] ء stays 'ʾ'. Words are unaffected (أَنَا stays 'anā').

When a space-separated run of bare single letters inside prose is expanded to letter names (SEAT/letter-name map in src/lang/ar/tap.ts ~line 357, proseTranslit), join the names with ', ' instead of a space. Examples: letters.json [28].sound '(أ إ ؤ ئ)' → '(alif with hamza, alif with hamza below, wāw with hamza, yāʾ with hamza)' (now run together with spaces, audit/letters-pronunciation.txt:607); a run like 'ف ع ل' → 'fāʾ, ʿayn, lām' if expanded the same way; a single letter or letters already separated by 'or'/',' ('a seat: أ or ؤ' → 'alif with hamza or wāw with hamza', tap-test.ts:74) are unchanged.
